items.stem: Why is it recommended to assign permissions to groups rather than individual users in Active Directory?

options.text: It simplifies management and keeps access consistent as people change roles
options.rationale: Correct: group-based access scales and is easier to audit.

options.text: Individual users cannot be given any permissions
options.rationale: Users can be assigned permissions; groups are simply better practice.
Groups do not disable auditing; they aid it.

options.text: It removes the need for a domain controller
options.rationale: Domain controllers are still required regardless of group use.

items.explanation: Correct: group-based permissions scale and stay consistent through role changes.

items.stem: Which TWO services must be healthy for domain logons to work reliably? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: clients use DNS to locate domain controllers.
Correct: authentication requires a contactable domain controller.
A public web server is unrelated to domain authentication.
Printing services are not required for logon.

items.explanation: Correct: DNS and a reachable domain controller are both essential for logons.

items.stem: A Group Policy Object is linked at both the domain and an OU with conflicting settings. By default, which applies to objects in that OU?

options.text: The OU-linked GPO, because the closest link in the processing order wins
options.rationale: Correct: GPOs apply site, domain, then OU, with the last applied normally winning.

options.text: The domain-linked GPO always overrides the OU
options.rationale: Unless enforced, the OU link applies later and normally wins.
Both are processed; the conflict is resolved by order.

options.text: The user must choose which applies
options.rationale: Policy application is automatic, not user-selected.

items.explanation: Correct: in default processing the OU-linked GPO applies last and wins.
